gaps: Correctly named the Upgrade: websocket header, but described the server-side mechanism for persistence as application-level ping/pong heartbeats (which actually solve a downstream NAT/LB idle-timeout problem) rather than the core fact: the server responds 101 Switching Protocols and drops HTTP's request/response turn-taking, holding the same TCP connection open indefinitely.

On a second attempt, described this as the server 'making the TCP connection full duplex' — TCP connections are already full-duplex by default; the actual change is at the application layer (HTTP's one-request-one-response discipline is dropped), not the transport layer.
